questions.question: A long straight wire carries $I = 10\ \mathrm{A}$. Find the magnetic field at a distance $r = 0.05\ \mathrm{m}$ from the wire. ($\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{T\cdot m/A}$)

Two long parallel wires are $d = 0.2\ \mathrm{m}$ apart. Wire 1 carries $I_1 = 5\ \mathrm{A}$ and Wire 2 carries $I_2 = 8\ \mathrm{A}$ in the same direction. Find: (a) the force per unit length between the wires, (b) attractive or repulsive?
questions.answer:
**(a)** $\dfrac{F}{L} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 5 \times 8}{2\pi \times 0.2}$

$= \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 40}{2\pi \times 0.2} = \dfrac{4\times10^{-6} \times 40}{0.4} = \dfrac{1.6\times10^{-4}}{0.4} = 4\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{N/m}$

**(b)** Parallel currents in the same direction $\Rightarrow$ **attractive**.

questions.question: At a point P located $r = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ from Wire 1 ($I_1 = 6\ \mathrm{A}$, into page) and $r = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ from Wire 2 ($I_2 = 6\ \mathrm{A}$, out of page), and P is equidistant between the wires. Find the net magnetic field at P.
questions.answer:
Both wires are $r = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ from P.

Each wire creates field: $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 6}{2\pi \times 0.1} = 1.2\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T}$

Wire 1 (into page): field at P circles clockwise around wire 1 — at P (if P is to the right of wire 1), field points **downward**.

Wire 2 (out of page): field at P circles counterclockwise around wire 2 — at P (if P is to the left of wire 2), field also points **downward**.

Both fields point in the same direction: $B_{\text{net}} = 2 \times 1.2\times10^{-5} = 2.4\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T}$

(Direction depends on exact geometry — assuming P is directly between the wires, both fields add up.)

questions.question: A solenoid has $n = 1000\ \mathrm{turns/m}$ and carries $I = 2\ \mathrm{A}$. Find the magnetic field inside the solenoid.
questions.answer:
Inside an ideal solenoid:

$B = \mu_0 n I = 4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 1000 \times 2$

$= 4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 2000 = 8\pi\times10^{-4} \approx 2.51\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{T} \approx 2.51\ \mathrm{mT}$

questions.question: Two long straight parallel wires, each carrying $I = 4\ \mathrm{A}$ in opposite directions, are $d = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ apart. Find the magnetic field at the midpoint between them.
questions.answer:
Both wires are $r = d/2 = 0.05\ \mathrm{m}$ from the midpoint.

$B_1 = B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 4}{2\pi \times 0.05} = \dfrac{1.6\times10^{-6}}{0.1} = 1.6\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T}$

For anti-parallel currents: at the midpoint, both magnetic fields point in the **same direction** (use right-hand rule for each — they add):

$B_{\text{net}} = 2B_1 = 3.2\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T} = 32\ \mu\mathrm{T}$

questions.question: Derive the formula $B = \mu_0 I/(2\pi r)$ for the magnetic field around a long straight wire using Ampère's Law.
questions.answer:
**Ampère's Law:** $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{\ell} = \mu_0 I_{\text{enc}}$

Choose a circular Amperian loop of radius $r$ centered on the wire (by symmetry, $B$ is constant in magnitude and tangent to this circle):

$B \oint d\ell = B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 I$

$$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$$ ✓

The right-hand rule (thumb in direction of $I$, fingers curl in direction of $\vec{B}$) gives the direction.

questions.question: A current $I = 15\ \mathrm{A}$ flows in a circular loop of radius $R = 0.05\ \mathrm{m}$. Find the magnetic field at the center of the loop.
questions.answer:
For a circular current loop, the field at the center is:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 15}{2 \times 0.05}$

$= \dfrac{6\pi\times10^{-6}}{0.1} = 6\pi\times10^{-5} \approx 1.885\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{T} \approx 188\ \mu\mathrm{T}$

questions.question: A long wire carries $I_1 = 20\ \mathrm{A}$. A second wire is placed parallel, $r = 0.04\ \mathrm{m}$ away, carrying $I_2 = 5\ \mathrm{A}$ in the opposite direction. Find: (a) the force per unit length on wire 2, (b) the direction of the force.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $\dfrac{F}{L} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi r} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 20 \times 5}{2\pi \times 0.04}$

$= \dfrac{4\times10^{-7} \times 100}{0.04 \times 2} = \dfrac{4\times10^{-5}}{0.08} = 5\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{N/m}$

**(b)** Antiparallel currents $\Rightarrow$ **repulsive** force (wire 2 is pushed away from wire 1).

questions.question: A toroid has $N = 400$ turns, mean radius $R = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$, and carries $I = 3\ \mathrm{A}$. Find the magnetic field inside the toroid.
questions.answer:
Apply Ampère's Law with a circular loop of radius $R$ inside the toroid:

$B(2\pi R) = \mu_0 N I$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I}{2\pi R} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 400 \times 3}{2\pi \times 0.1}$

$= \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 1200}{0.2\pi} = \dfrac{4\times10^{-7} \times 1200}{0.2} = 2.4\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{T} = 2.4\ \mathrm{mT}$

questions.question: Two wires are perpendicular to each other and cross in the same plane. Wire 1 (horizontal) carries $I_1 = 10\ \mathrm{A}$ to the right. Wire 2 (vertical) carries $I_2 = 8\ \mathrm{A}$ upward. Find the magnitude and direction of the magnetic field at a point P located $0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ to the right of wire 2 and $0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ above wire 1 (i.e., at the corner of a square).
questions.answer:
P is $r_1 = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ from wire 1 (above it) and $r_2 = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ from wire 2 (to the right).

**From wire 1** ($I_1$ to the right): right-hand rule gives $B_1$ **out of page** at P (P is above wire 1)

$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi r_1} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 10}{2\pi \times 0.1} = 2\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T}$ (out of page)

**From wire 2** ($I_2$ upward): right-hand rule gives $B_2$ **out of page** at P (P is to the right of wire 2)

$B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_2}{2\pi r_2} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 8}{2\pi \times 0.1} = 1.6\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T}$ (out of page)

Both fields are in the same direction: $B_{\text{net}} = (2.0 + 1.6)\times10^{-5} = 3.6\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T}$ (out of page)
